lede: Buffalo had last change, so Lindy Ruff picked most of these matchups. Buffalo played without Ryan McLeod and Louis Crevier. Columbus played without Ryan Lomberg and Luca Del Bel Belluz.

notes.head: The third line drew Knies’s line
notes.text: Lindy Ruff sent Kulich, Norris and Zucker out for 5:11 of their 7:54 at 5-on-5 against Knies, Fantilli and Garland (66%, about 32% with no line matching), and the chances were close, 0.15 to 0.24 expected goals.

notes.head: The fourth line drew Voronkov’s line
notes.text: Malenstyn, Kozak and Carrick spent 4:01 of their 7:50 at 5-on-5 against Voronkov, Williams and Lorentz (51%, about 20% with no line matching).

notes.head: Quinn’s line drew Coyle’s line
notes.text: Doan, Östlund and Quinn spent 4:37 of their 8:45 at 5-on-5 against Sillinger, Coyle and Olivier (53%, about 26% with no line matching), and the chances were close, 0.61 to 0.70 expected goals. Buffalo scored one of its five goals then.

notes.head: One matchup paid off
notes.text: Benson, Krebs and Thompson kept drawing Columbus’s first line, Knies, Fantilli and Garland. In those 3:50 Buffalo had 0.35 expected goals to Columbus’s 0.00. Buffalo scored one of its five goals then.

foot: Lindy Ruff matched about as hard as in his other home games: each line spent 41% of its time against one opposing line, against 35% to 45% in his first six.
